newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SOCCER-DE BILDE BANNED FOR PUNCHING OPPONENT IN FACE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DE BILDE BANNED FOR PUNCHING OPPONENT IN FACE.

text.p: Belgium and Anderlecht striker Gilles De Bilde was banned from playing until March 31 on Wednesday for punching another player in the face, the Belgian soccer union said.

De Bilde, who was charged with assault and grievous bodily harm after striking Aalst's Krist Porte during the game on December 21, expressed his regrets after the ruling of the soccer union's sports committee.
"I regret what has happened and respect the decision of the committee," De Bilde said.
He spent a night in jail after the incident, which left Porte with a broken eye socket and nose, and was suspended until further notice by both by his club and the soccer union.
De Bilde's lawyers and Anderlecht said they would not appeal against the soccer union's decision.
Earlier, de Bilde's lawyers had argued that Porte had provoked the Anderlecht striker prior to the punch and that the media had made too much of the incident.
The soccer union turned down a request by Aalst to have the match, which they lost 3-0, replayed.
De Bilde, who will miss 10 league games and two Belgian Cup matches, had already publicly apologised to Porte and Anderlecht fans in a prime-time television show last week.
Porte still stuffers from blurred vision and headaches and has to rest for at least two more weeks before undergoing any further treatment.
De Bilde, who moved to Anderlecht from Aalst in 1995 after turning down a lucrative offer from Atletico Madrid, became a national celebrity when he won the 1994 award for best Belgian league player.
Belgian media said earlier on Wednesday that leading Dutch club PSV Eindhoven were keen to sign De Bilde, regardless of whether he was suspended.
But FIFA, the game's world governing body, has made it clear that a player cannot be transferred to a foreign club when serving a ban.
De Bilde, who felled Porte with a left hook in front of television cameras, faces trial for another alleged assault.
He allegedly struck two male nurses in August 1995 when he was denied access to his father in hospital. 221956 GMT jan 97
